How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Above a Fireplace

How to Hang and Style Artwork for the Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall that gets good natural or artificial light and where the prints will be at eye level when you're seated — above a sofa, beside a reading chair or over a console table are all great spots for this set.

2. Measure your space: Hold the three prints up against the wall (or use paper cut-outs the same size) to check they'll fill roughly two-thirds of the wall width. Mark the centre point of your display with a light pencil dot.

3. Map out the layout: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall to plan your spacing. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks balanced — close enough to read as a set, with enough breathing room to appreciate each one individually.

4. Hang the centre print first: Fix the middle print at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is the standard guide). Use a spirit level to make sure it's straight.

5. Add the outer prints: Working outwards from the centre, hang the left and right prints at exactly the same height, maintaining your chosen gap. Step back and check the alignment — adjust as needed before any marks become permanent.

6. Style around them: These prints work beautifully with warm-toned accessories — think natural wood, wicker baskets, a cosy throw or a small stack of real books on a shelf below. Let the art lead the room's colour story.

Look and feel — Unframed print: flexible — suits any frame style you choose. Framed print: clean, polished, gallery-ready finish. Wrapped canvas: painterly, textured, gallery-wrap appearance with no frame required.

Best for — Unframed print: those who already have frames or want full control over the framing style. Framed print: anyone who wants a fuss-free, complete result. Wrapped canvas: those who love a natural, painted-art aesthetic on the wall.

A 3 piece wall art framed set is a group of three coordinating art prints designed to be displayed together as a single arrangement on your wall. How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Framed Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall: Start by measuring the width of your chimney breast or the wall space above your fireplace. As a guide, aim for the full spread of all three prints to cover roughly two thirds of that width — this keeps things balanced and stops the set looking too small or too crowded.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of the wall and mark it lightly with a pencil. The middle print should sit centred on this point, with the two flanking prints placed at an even distance on either side — a gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks neat and intentional.

4. Use a spirit level: Before you hammer any nails, use a spirit level or a free smartphone app to make sure all three prints are perfectly aligned horizontally. Even a small tilt can make the whole arrangement look off, so it's worth taking an extra minute here.

5. Step back and adjust: Once hung, step back and look at the set from across the room — this is the view most people will have. Small tweaks to spacing or height at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

What is bar wall art decor?

Bar wall art decor refers to printed artwork designed to bring personality and style to a home bar area, bar cart, or any living space with a drinks or entertaining theme. It typically features cocktail illustrations, liquor bottles, wine motifs, vintage bar signs or retro drink recipes, and is sold as single prints or coordinated sets. This set of 3 pastel cocktail prints is a popular choice because the soft, fresh colour palette and clean modern typography work equally well in a dedicated home bar corner or a general living room. Choosing a matching set means you get a cohesive, gallery-ready look without having to source individual pieces separately.

How to Hang Bar Wall Art Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick the wall you want to use — above a sofa, a bar cart or a sideboard works brilliantly. Measure the width of the space and divide by three to work out roughly how wide each print should be, leaving equal gaps between them.

2. Select your size and finish: Decide whether you want a smaller, more delicate arrangement or a larger, bolder statement. Luster paper suits rooms with natural light; Museum quality paper suits brighter or more formal spaces; wrapped canvas suits a contemporary, frameless look.

3. Mark your hanging points: Hold the first print up to the wall at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is a good guide). Mark lightly with a pencil. Repeat for the other two, keeping the gaps even — around 5–8 cm between each print is ideal.

4. Hang and level: Use appropriate wall fixings for your wall type. Once all three are up, use a spirit level to check they are aligned, and step back to make sure the spacing looks even from a distance.

5. Style around them: Add a drinks tray, some glassware or a small plant on a shelf or bar cart below the prints to tie the whole look together and really make the bar wall art decor sing.

Comparing Your Options: Which Format Suits You Best?

Format — Unframed Print: You receive the art print only, ready for you to frame in a frame of your own choosing. Perfect if you already have frames or want to match existing decor precisely.

Format — Framed Print: The print arrives ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no need to source a separate frame. A great time-saver and the most popular choice for gifting.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, frameless look. Ideal for modern or minimalist interiors.

Paper — Luster Art Paper: A semi-gloss finish that makes colours appear vibrant and rich. Works beautifully in rooms with natural light where you want the pastel tones to really glow.

Paper — Museum Quality Paper: A premium matt finish with a refined, gallery-like feel. A great choice if your room gets strong direct light or if you prefer a more understated, sophisticated look.
